title: OVAT
subtitle: OpenVINO Agentic Toolkit for AI PCs
summary: Turns agent boilerplate into one YAML file and one command. OVAT runs tool-calling agents on Intel AI PCs against OpenVINO Model Server: describe the model, the tools, and the agent in workflow.yml, then ovat run does the rest.
body:
A simple tool-calling agent against OpenVINO Model Server is really fifty lines of boilerplate: build the client, hand-write every tool's JSON schema, check finish_reason, dispatch the tool, append the result, loop, and babysit the message history. Every new agent copy-pastes that and slowly diverges.

OVAT collapses all of it into a small workflow.yml and one command:

  ovat run workflow.yml --input "What do my notes say about Q3?"

WHAT IT HANDLES
model wiring to OVMS (device, tool parser, endpoints)
tool schemas generated from plain Python functions
the agent loop, iteration guards, and history management

It targets Intel AI PCs, with the GPU or NPU doing the heavy lifting. Python under the hood, YAML at the surface, no framework lock-in.

title: OvaSearch
subtitle: Native C++ multimodal RAG engine
summary: A local-first multimodal retrieval engine. Text, PDFs, and images flow through OpenVINO's VLM and text-embedding pipelines into a USearch HNSW index, with zero-copy image ingestion and a sliding-window chunker, all in portable C++.
body:
A retrieval-augmented generation engine that runs natively in C++, accelerated by Intel OpenVINO. Built for low-latency multimodal search across text, image, and audio embeddings without a Python runtime in the hot path.

BY THE NUMBERS
embedding dim: 384
retrieval p50: ~6 ms
index: USearch HNSW
runtime: OpenVINO CPU

WHY C++
Most multimodal RAG stacks assume Python and a stack of model-serving daemons. OvaSearch is a single binary that wires VLMPipeline, TextEmbeddingPipeline, and LLMPipeline from OpenVINO directly, with a custom ImageAllocator for zero-copy image ingestion. No framework tax, no Python hop. That matters when you actually run this on a laptop.

INDEXING SHAPE
Text and PDFs flow through a sliding-window chunker (1000 characters, 200 overlap). Images are captioned once by a Qwen2-VL pipeline and then chunked like any other document. A flat-file cache stores chunks, embeddings, and sources so cold-start reads are deterministic.

HOT PATH (sketch)
  // Retrieve top-k by cosine, then assemble context for the LLM
  auto query = embed(question);                    // bge-small-en-v1.5 via OpenVINO
  auto hits  = index.search(query, /*top_k=*/5);   // USearch HNSW
  for (auto& h : hits) {
    if (h.distance > 0.45f) continue;              // relevance floor
    ctx.append(store.chunk_at(h.key), store.source_of(h.key));
  }
  llm.stream(build_prompt(ctx, question));         // Llama-3.2-3B INT4

WHAT'S NEXT
Video and audio ingestion via keyframe sampling and whisper.cpp, hybrid lexical plus semantic retrieval with BM25 and RRF, and an NPU/GPU switch for AI PC deployment.

title: Lisper
subtitle: Local transcription studio on whisper.cpp + C++
summary: A modular C++ speech-to-text tool built on whisper.cpp. Clean API boundaries let it slot in as a tool for agentic pipelines, a library for editors, or a standalone CLI. No cloud call, no Python, no surprises.
body:
A native transcription studio wrapping whisper.cpp, with a workflow for batch jobs, edit-as-you-listen review, and speaker labeling, all running on the device.

THE IDEA
Every transcription tool I tried was either a wrapper around a cloud API or a GUI hiding whisper.cpp behind Electron. Lisper is the opposite: a small, modular C++ layer on top of whisper.cpp with a clean API that can be registered as an agentic tool or called as a library.

SHAPE
The transcription pipeline, the model loader, and the I/O front-ends are separate compilation units, so embedders pull exactly the pieces they need. The same codebase ships a CLI, a library surface, and eventually an editor plug-in.

STATS
runtime: whisper.cpp
language: C++
deps: CMake only

Built out of frustration with web tools that ship your audio off your machine. Lisper keeps everything local: drag in audio, get a clean transcript with timestamps, edit, export.
